about.valuesTitle: Three things you can count on.
about.valuesBody: These are non-negotiable. They shape every engagement and how I price the work.
about.value1Body: I quote line items after the scoping call and the contract freezes them. If scope changes mid-build, I flag it before doing extra work, not after. No surprise invoices.
about.value2Body: Code in your GitHub, design files in your Figma, workflows as portable JSON, credentials in your password manager. Nothing lives in my accounts. Handover is a non-event.
about.value3Body: Every Friday you get a working demo, not a Slack message. Work ships in slices — you see it in production, you react, we adjust. No "we are on track" without a link.
about.hoursBody: Mon–Fri · 8 a.m.–6 p.m. GMT-5. I respond in under 24 h on business days. I do not bill by the hour — every engagement is a fixed-price contract.

servicesHub.tracksSubtitle: Each track stands on its own. They get sharper when combined — an audit informs the build, the build informs the UX, and the UX drives the next round of automation.
servicesHub.track1Summary: Repetitive work, off the team's plate. AI agents, no-code flows, and custom integrations that pay for themselves — measured in hours, not hype.
servicesHub.track1Cap2: AI agents and chatbots on streaming APIs
servicesHub.track2Summary: Interfaces that feel obvious and convert. Research, design, and iterate — until the user doesn't have to think twice.

servicesHub.processTitle: The same three steps, every project.
servicesHub.processSubtitle: Whether I'm building an automation flow, a design system, or a SaaS front end, the rhythm is the same.
servicesHub.process1Desc: Map the current state — workflows, screens, conversion paths. The cheapest step to skip, the most expensive one to skip.
servicesHub.process2Desc: Small, observable pieces. Every flow has a dashboard, every error has an alert, every retry has a story. No big-bang relaunches.
servicesHub.process3Desc: Watch what real users do and tune. The first version is the start of the conversation, not the end of the project.
servicesHub.diffTitle: A background that compounds on the brief.
servicesHub.diffSubtitle: The four edges that show up in the work, not just the headline.
servicesHub.diff1Desc: I've closed deals across LATAM. Empathy for the customer, sharp eye for the numbers.
servicesHub.diff2Desc: Versioned prompts, the way code should be. No black boxes, no hidden lock-in.
servicesHub.diff3Desc: Wireframes first, pixels second. I sit with engineering, review every PR, and tune live.
servicesHub.diff4Desc: TypeScript on the front, validated payloads on every API. Bugs stay rare, features stay fast.

servicesAi.caseDesc: AI agents that bulk-upload products, write SEO copy, and ship to marketplaces — what used to be a 90-minute manual task now finishes in 15.
servicesAi.caseImageAlt: E-commerce automation case: products uploaded in bulk by an AI agent
servicesAi.cap1Desc: I sit with your team and map every repetitive step — from inbox triage to intake to fulfillment. The audit ends with a prioritized backlog of automations ranked by ROI.
servicesAi.cap2Desc: Conversational agents that answer customer questions, qualify leads, and route work to the right human. Built on OpenAI, Anthropic, or open-source models via streaming APIs.
servicesAi.cap3Desc: No-code and low-code flows that connect your CRM, email, calendar, sheets, and SaaS tools. Trigger to action, end to end, with logging and retry handling.
servicesAi.cap4Desc: Bulk product uploads, AI-generated descriptions and images from phone snapshots, and multi-platform publishing. The 90→15 minute case study from the portfolio — engineered for real stores.
servicesAi.cap5Desc: AI-driven scraping, enrichment, and personalized cold outreach that reads like a 1:1 message. Warm leads land in your CRM, ready for your sales team to close.
servicesAi.cap6Desc: Webhooks, REST and GraphQL APIs, OAuth flows, background jobs. When the SaaS you need doesn't exist, I build the bridge that does the job.
servicesAi.approachSubtitle: Five steps, every project. The same rhythm whether the deliverable is a saved hour or a shipped product.
servicesAi.approach1Desc: Every project starts with the workflow, not the tool. I dig into how your team actually works today, where time is leaking, and which automations pay for themselves in weeks — not quarters.
servicesAi.approach2Desc: Once the backlog is locked, I ship in small, observable pieces. Every flow has a dashboard, every error has an alert, every retry has a story.
servicesAi.approach3Desc: I treat prompts like code: version-controlled, evaluated against golden datasets, and rolled back when they drift. No black boxes on my watch.
servicesAi.approach4Desc: Your data stays where it belongs. Self-hosted models when privacy or cost demands it, third-party APIs when speed to ship matters more.
servicesAi.approach5Desc: After launch, I monitor what real traffic teaches and iterate. The first version is the start of the conversation, not the end of the project.

servicesUiUx.capabilitiesTitle: What I bring to the table
servicesUiUx.cap1Desc: User interviews, surveys, usability testing, and competitive analysis. I dig into real behavior so the design follows from evidence, not assumptions.
servicesUiUx.cap2Desc: End-to-end flows that make the next step obvious. Wireframes that lock down structure before pixels take over.
servicesUiUx.cap3Desc: Production-ready UI in Figma with type, color, and spacing systems. Components that hold up at any screen size.
servicesUiUx.cap4Desc: Every screen has a job. I iterate on copy, layout, and CTA hierarchy so the path to conversion is short and obvious.
servicesUiUx.cap5Desc: Tokens, components, and documentation so design and engineering speak the same language. Less drift, faster shipping.
servicesUiUx.cap6Desc: Moderated and unmoderated sessions. Real users, real tasks, real metrics. I turn findings into a backlog your dev team can actually act on.
servicesUiUx.approachSubtitle: Five steps, every project. The same rhythm whether the deliverable is a one-screen fix or a full product redesign.
servicesUiUx.approach1Desc: I start by understanding the user and the business at the same time — neither one matters without the other. Empathy for the customer, sharp eye for the numbers.
servicesUiUx.approach2Desc: Once I've mapped the journey and locked the flow, I move fast on wireframes. Cheap to change, expensive to skip.
servicesUiUx.approach3Desc: Visual design comes after the structure is solid. I build a clear type and spacing system so screens feel consistent without being repetitive.
servicesUiUx.approach4Desc: Every interface gets tested. Five users catch 85% of usability problems, and the rest gets folded into the next sprint.
servicesUiUx.approach5Desc: Design doesn't stop at handoff. I sit with engineering, review every PR, and tune the live product when real-world data comes in.

privacy.metaDescription: How I collect, use, and protect your data on andresmorales.com.co.
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data I collect when you use andresmorales.com.co, why I collect it, and what I do with it. I keep it short on purpose.
privacy.dataCollectedBody: When you submit the contact form or project brief, I receive the information you type (name, email, project details) plus technical metadata (IP address, timestamp, user agent) for spam protection. Plausible Analytics records anonymized page views without cookies or personal identifiers.
privacy.whyBody: To reply to your message, deliver the work we agreed on, prevent spam and abuse, and understand which pages are useful. I never sell your data. I never share it with third parties for marketing.
privacy.thirdPartiesBody: Contact form submissions are emailed via Brevo (transactional email, EU-hosted). Project briefs also create a task in ClickUp (project management, US-hosted). Both processors are bound by data-processing agreements. Plausible Analytics is cookieless and self-hosted in the EU.
privacy.retentionBody: Form submissions stay in my inbox until the project is finished and invoiced, then archived for tax records. You can ask me to delete them earlier.
privacy.rightsBody: Under Colombia's Ley 1581/2012, Brazil's LGPD, and the EU's GDPR, you can request access, correction, deletion, or portability of your data at any time. Email info@andresmorales.com.co and I will respond within 15 business days.
privacy.changesBody: If I update this page I will change the date above. Material changes will be announced on the home page.
privacy.contactBody: Email info@andresmorales.com.co. I am the data controller.

makeVsN8n.tldr:
I've shipped 87 workflows on n8n since 2025 — 24 running daily. I've tested Make but never shipped one to production. Here's the honest comparison.

n8n if your team writes code or wants self-hosting; Make if your team is non-technical and you want polish over flexibility. Both run production workflows at scale — pick by team, not by feature list.
makeVsN8n.tableIntro: Four criteria that actually decide it.

rows.winner: n8n for teams that can self-host

criteria.title: Pricing — what you actually pay
criteria.body: Make bills per operation, so a workflow that fans out to five systems costs five credits per run. Heavy automations scale the bill faster than people expect. n8n is free when self-hosted; the cloud tier starts around $24/month with predictable per-execution pricing. If your team already runs its own infra, n8n is dramatically cheaper at scale.

criteria.title: Hosting and data residency
criteria.body: Make runs entirely on Make infrastructure. n8n can run on your laptop, a $5 VPS, or n8n Cloud. For LATAM teams with data residency requirements or sensitive customer data, self-hosting n8n removes a class of compliance questions before they start.

criteria.title: Learning curve — who can build workflows
criteria.body: Make is genuinely easier for non-developers; the visual editor is one of the best in the category. n8n rewards teams comfortable with code — JS expressions, HTTP nodes, and a real data flow concept — and is steeper for pure no-code users. Hiring signals matter: if your team is half developers, n8n compounds; if not, Make ships faster.

x: Your team is mostly non-technical and you need to ship automations this week.
You want a polished UI and the widest catalog of pre-built app integrations.
You can model the cost as a predictable operations line item.
y: Your team writes code and you want full control over logic and data.
You need self-hosting for data residency, cost, or compliance reasons.
You plan to integrate with custom APIs or build reusable components.

faqs.question: Is n8n really free?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you self-host it. The fair-code license lets you run, modify, and keep your workflows without paying n8n. n8n Cloud plans start around $24/month and remove the ops work of hosting it yourself.

faqs.question: Does Make scale for production workloads?
faqs.answer: Yes. Make runs in production at companies processing millions of operations per month. The ceiling is operational cost and governance, not capability — plan your credit budget the same way you would any cloud bill.

faqs.question: Can I migrate from Make to n8n (or vice versa)?
faqs.answer: Yes, but workflows do not port directly. Both tools import and export JSON; plan one to two weeks of rebuild time per major workflow, plus testing. Keep credentials out of the migration scope — export them once and reuse.

aiVsAgency.metaTitle: AI consultant vs agency — honest 2026 comparison
aiVsAgency.metaDescription: AI consultant vs agency: when to hire solo technical help and when you need a full agency team. Cost, speed, hands-on work and strategy — compared.
aiVsAgency.h1: AI consultant vs agency: which one for your AI automation project?
aiVsAgency.subtitle: Both ship AI work. The trade-off is hands-on technical depth versus broader strategy capacity and team scale.
aiVsAgency.tldr: Hire a solo AI consultant when you need hands-on n8n/Make work, custom integrations, and direct technical accountability. Hire an agency when you need a broader marketing/strategy layer or a larger team for ongoing campaigns.

rows.x: Yes — the person you talk to builds it

criteria.title: Cost structure and what you actually pay for
criteria.body: A solo consultant quotes a fixed scope against deliverables — code, workflows, integrations, a working demo. Agencies price against retainers that bundle strategy, account management, and a delivery team. For pure technical AI work, the consultant dollar travels further. The math flips when you need creative, content, or paid media running in parallel.

criteria.title: Speed to first output
criteria.body: Consultants typically ship a working demo in one to two weeks; the first call is the scoping call, the first Friday is a live demo. Agencies usually spend four to eight weeks in kickoff: strategy docs, account plans, and team onboarding before production work starts. If you need to prove value quickly, consultants win on velocity.

criteria.title: Hands-on technical accountability
criteria.body: With a consultant, the person you hired is the person writing the workflow, deploying the integration, and fixing the bug at 11pm. With an agency, the senior who sold the work is rarely the one building it. If the deliverable is technical and breaks are expensive, the direct-accountability model is safer.

x: The deliverable is technical — automations, integrations, AI features — not marketing campaigns.
You want the person who scoped the work to also build it.
You need a working demo in the next two weeks, not a proposal deck.
y: You need creative, content, paid media, and engineering running in parallel.
Your roadmap spans brand strategy, campaign execution, and technical build-outs.
You need a full team for sustained output over many months.

faqs.question: When does a solo consultant hit a ceiling?
faqs.answer: When scope crosses into marketing, brand strategy, or sustained campaign execution at scale. For pure technical AI work — automations, integrations, internal tools — a senior consultant scales further per dollar than an agency team. The ceiling shows up when you need creative, content, and paid media running in parallel with engineering.

faqs.question: How do I verify an AI consultant actually ships?
faqs.answer: Ask for working demos in production, not pitch decks or Looms. A weekly demo cadence is the test: if they are shipping, you see it live on Friday. Anything else — mocked screenshots, recorded walkthroughs, "we are finishing it next week" — is a yellow flag.

faqs.question: What happens if I outgrow a consultant?
faqs.answer: You own everything: code, design files, workflows, credentials, documentation. Handover is a non-event because there is nothing locked behind their account. You can hire a different consultant or build an in-house team without paying a transfer fee or losing access.

vercelVsAmplify.metaTitle: Vercel vs AWS Amplify for Next.js — 2026
vercelVsAmplify.metaDescription: Vercel vs AWS Amplify for Next.js in 2026: DX, pricing at scale, lock-in and edge performance compared. Pick by stage, not by hype.
vercelVsAmplify.h1: Vercel vs AWS Amplify for Next.js: when each one wins
vercelVsAmplify.subtitle: Both deploy Next.js to production. The choice is developer experience versus AWS-native cost control at scale.
vercelVsAmplify.tldr: Vercel for Next.js apps where DX and time-to-deploy matter. AWS Amplify when you are already deep in AWS or need fine-grained cost control at scale. Both run Next.js in production.
vercelVsAmplify.tableIntro: Four criteria that move the needle.

rows.x: Native — built by the Next.js team
rows.y: Good, but more setup and config

criteria.title: Next.js developer experience
criteria.body: Vercel is built by the team behind Next.js, so framework features — Server Components, App Router, ISR, Edge Runtime — work the day they ship. Amplify caught up in 2024 and supports App Router and SSR well, but you will write more configuration: build commands, runtime selection, and edge function setup are not as automated. For prototype-to-Series-A, the Vercel DX saves hours.

criteria.title: Pricing at scale
criteria.body: Vercel Pro starts at $20/seat/month and bandwidth costs add up fast on high-traffic sites. Amplify bills against AWS infrastructure — you pay for what you provision, and Savings Plans or reserved capacity can drop costs by 30 to 60 percent at scale. For pre-PMF products, Vercel economics are fine. For products at scale, run the numbers.

criteria.title: Lock-in and portability
criteria.body: Vercel-specific features — Edge Config, KV, the proprietary image loader — tie you to the platform. Amplify deploys standard Next.js output to standard AWS infrastructure, so leaving AWS is a normal cloud migration rather than a rewrite. If multi-cloud or portability matters, Amplify is the safer long-term home.

x: You ship fast and value framework-native DX over infrastructure knobs.
Your team is small and does not want to manage AWS infra.
You need edge runtime and ISR working out of the box.
y: You are already deep in AWS and want one bill, one IAM model, one VPC.
Cost at scale is a first-order constraint — high traffic, tight margins.
Portability and standard infrastructure matter for your exit options.

faqs.question: Can I migrate from Vercel to Amplify later?
faqs.answer: Yes, with effort. Next.js itself is framework-agnostic, so the application code moves cleanly. The lock-in is at the platform layer: env vars, edge config, image optimization, build pipeline. Plan one to two weeks for a non-trivial migration, plus testing against production traffic.

faqs.question: Is Vercel's premium pricing worth it?
faqs.answer: For prototypes and pre-PMF products, almost always yes — the DX saves engineering hours that cost more than the bill. For products at scale, run the numbers: Amplify plus CloudFront plus reserved capacity can be 30 to 60 percent cheaper at sustained high traffic.

faqs.question: Does Amplify support the Next.js App Router fully?
faqs.answer: Yes, since 2024. Server Components, SSR, ISR, and the Edge Runtime all work. The setup is more manual than Vercel — you configure the runtime and build commands yourself — but the runtime support is mature and battle-tested.

process.heroTitle: Five steps from kickoff to iteration.
process.heroSubtitle: The same rhythm for every engagement, from a 1-week AI Kickstart to a 3-month AI Platform. No surprises, no scope creep — the contract freezes the line items on day 1 and the work ships on day N.
process.tracksTitle: Same five steps, three different shapes.
process.tracksSubtitle: AI / UX / Web each have their own cadence. The skeleton is identical; the bones change.
process.step1Body: 1 week of deep-dive. We map your current stack, the manual work that costs you the most, and the systems that already hold the data. Output: a 5-10 page audit doc with ranked opportunities and a fixed price per workflow.
process.step2Body: 30-min video call. I walk you through the audit and you pick 1-3 of the opportunities. Output: a one-page scope with line items, fixed price, and timeline. The contract freezes the work.
process.step3Body: 1-6 weeks depending on tier. I work in weekly slices — every Friday you get a working demo, not a status update. If scope changes mid-build, I flag it before doing extra work, never after.
process.step4Body: Deploy to production with eval and monitoring in place. You own every line of code, every API key, every workflow JSON. Nothing lives in my accounts.
process.step5Body: Optional retainer: monitoring, eval, prompt iteration, model updates, new workflow rollouts. 3-month minimum commitment, cancel anytime after. Most clients keep a small retainer to compound wins.

pricing.title: Honest ranges, no hidden quotes
pricing.subtitle: Three tiers per service. The exact price depends on scope — but the range is what most projects at each tier end up costing. Every engagement is a fixed-price quote after a 30-min scoping call, never an hourly invoice.
pricing.methodologyBody: Ranges are calibrated against 2025-2026 market data for senior independent AI / design / web consultants in the US and EU. They run 40-60% below what boutique firms in San Francisco, London or Berlin charge for the same scope — without sacrificing quality. Final price depends on scope, integrations and timeline. The scoping call is free and freezes the line items before any work starts.
pricing.aiT1Body: One workflow, one integration. Typically a single-channel automation (Slack + Sheets + OpenAI) or a custom chatbot. Ships in 1-2 weeks.
pricing.aiT2Body: Multi-workflow build (3-6 flows) with custom integrations (HubSpot, Pipedrive, Airtable, n8n, Wompi). Eval and production monitoring included. Ships in 3-6 weeks.
pricing.aiT3Body: Multi-agent system with custom integrations, SSO, eval harness, observability. Ships in 8-12 weeks. Includes a 90-day iteration window.
pricing.uxT1Body: Two-week design sprint: research, IA, key flows, clickable prototype, usability test. Output is a Figma file your team can ship from.
pricing.uxT2Body: End-to-end product design for a new feature or app: research, IA, design system, prototyping, dev handoff. Ships in 4-6 weeks.
pricing.uxT3Body: Ongoing design partnership: weekly cadence, design system stewardship, prototyping, and design QA on every release. 3-month minimum.
pricing.webT1Body: One-page Next.js site with copy, design system, deployment, analytics, and a contact form. Ships in 1-2 weeks.
pricing.webT2Body: Multi-page Next.js site: home, services, portfolio, contact, CMS-driven blog, i18n. Ships in 3-5 weeks.
pricing.webT3Body: Custom platform with auth, database, payments, admin panel. Includes architecture, implementation, deployment, and monitoring. Ships in 6-10 weeks.
pricing.retainerBody: After the build, an optional monthly retainer covers monitoring, prompt iteration, model updates, eval, and new workflow rollouts. 3-month minimum, cancel anytime after.
pricing.rangesCaveat: These ranges are calibrated against market data for senior independent consultants in the US and EU. Final price depends on scope, integrations, and timeline — every engagement is a fixed-price quote after the scoping call, never an hourly invoice.
